points.title: 早年成长与文学启蒙
points.description: 奥克塔维奥·帕斯出生于墨西哥城一个政治活跃的家庭，祖父是自由派政治家，父亲是律师和记者。他在墨西哥城度过了童年和青少年时期，接受了良好的教育。这一时期，帕斯开始接触墨西哥革命后的文化氛围，深受墨西哥现代主义诗人如何塞·胡安·塔布拉达的影响。1928年，14岁的帕斯发表了第一首诗作。1933年，他创办了文学杂志《巴别塔》，并开始与墨西哥前卫艺术圈交往，包括迭戈·里维拉和弗里达·卡罗等艺术家。这段经历奠定了他日后文学创作和思想发展的基础。
points.descriptionEn: Octavio Paz was born in Mexico City to a politically active family; his grandfather was a liberal politician and his father a lawyer and journalist. He spent his childhood and adolescence in Mexico City, receiving an excellent education. During this period, Paz was exposed to the cultural atmosphere following the Mexican Revolution and was deeply influenced by Mexican modernist poets like José Juan Tablada. In 1928, at age 14, Paz published his first poem. In 1933, he founded the literary magazine 'Babel' and began associating with Mexico's avant-garde art circles, including Diego Rivera and Frida Kahlo. These experiences laid the foundation for his future literary and intellectual development.

points.title: 玛雅文化研究
points.description: 1937年，帕斯前往尤卡坦半岛，在梅里达的一所学校担任教师。这段经历使他深入接触了玛雅文化，并开始研究墨西哥的土著传统。他走访了玛雅遗址，收集民间传说，并将这些元素融入他的诗歌创作中。1943年，他出版了第一部重要诗集《荒野中的月亮》，展现了墨西哥土著文化对他的深刻影响。在尤卡坦半岛的岁月不仅丰富了他的文化视野，也形成了他后来对墨西哥身份认同的独特思考，他将墨西哥定义为东西方文化的交汇点，这一思想贯穿于他的整个创作生涯。
points.descriptionEn: In 1937, Paz traveled to the Yucatán Peninsula, where he worked as a teacher in Mérida. This experience allowed him to immerse himself in Mayan culture and begin studying Mexico's indigenous traditions. He visited Mayan archaeological sites, collected folk tales, and incorporated these elements into his poetry. In 1943, he published his first major collection of poems, 'The Moon in the Wilderness,' showing the profound influence of Mexican indigenous culture on his work. His years in Yucatán not only broadened his cultural perspective but also shaped his later unique thinking about Mexican identity, which he defined as a meeting point of Eastern and Western cultures—a theme that runs throughout his career.

points.title: 外交官与欧洲文化影响
points.description: 1945年，帕斯进入墨西哥外交部，被派驻巴黎，开始了他的外交官生涯。在巴黎，他接触了欧洲超现实主义和存在主义哲学，与安德烈·布勒东、阿尔贝托·贾科梅蒂等艺术家交往密切。这段经历极大地拓展了他的文化视野，使他能够从外部审视墨西哥文化。1951年，他出版了重要散文集《孤独的迷宫》，探讨了墨西哥人的心理和文化特征。1953-1959年间，帕斯在墨西哥驻纽约领事馆工作，随后返回巴黎担任墨西哥驻法国大使。这一时期，他的创作风格更加成熟，开始融合东西方思想，形成了独特的文化批评视角。
points.descriptionEn: In 1945, Paz entered the Mexican foreign service and was posted to Paris, beginning his diplomatic career. In Paris, he was exposed to European surrealism and existentialist philosophy and associated closely with artists like André Breton and Alberto Giacometti. This experience greatly expanded his cultural perspective, allowing him to examine Mexican culture from an external viewpoint. In 1951, he published his important essay collection 'The Labyrinth of Solitude,' exploring the psychological and cultural characteristics of Mexicans. Between 1953 and 1959, Paz worked at the Mexican consulate in New York, then returned to Paris as Mexico's ambassador to France. During this period, his writing style matured, and he began to synthesize Eastern and Western thought, forming a unique cultural critique perspective.

points.title: 特莱蒂洛科事件与政治觉醒
points.description: 1968年，帕斯担任墨西哥驻印度大使期间，墨西哥城爆发了学生抗议活动，随后政府军队在特莱蒂洛科广场对示威者进行了血腥镇压，造成数百人死亡。帕斯公开谴责了这一暴行，并辞去外交职务以示抗议。这一事件成为他政治生涯的转折点，使他更加关注墨西哥的政治现实和社会正义。他开始积极参与政治评论，批评墨西哥的一党专政制度。1970年，他创办了重要文学杂志《多元》，成为墨西哥知识界的重要平台。这一时期，他的创作更加关注政治和社会问题，将文学与政治紧密结合，体现了知识分子的社会责任感。
points.descriptionEn: In 1968, while serving as Mexico's ambassador to India, student protests erupted in Mexico City, followed by a brutal government crackdown at the Tlatelolco Plaza that killed hundreds of people. Paz publicly condemned this violence and resigned from his diplomatic post in protest. This event marked a turning point in his political career, making him more aware of Mexico's political realities and social justice issues. He began to actively engage in political commentary, criticizing Mexico's one-party system. In 1970, he founded the important literary magazine 'Vuelta,' which became a major platform for Mexican intellectuals. During this period, his writing became more focused on political and social issues, closely linking literature with politics and reflecting the social responsibility of intellectuals.

points.title: 文学巅峰与诺贝尔奖
points.description: 1976年后，帕斯回到墨西哥城，专注于文学创作和学术研究。这一时期是他创作的巅峰期，出版了多部重要作品，包括《东方的树叶》(1976)、《转折》(1977)和《诗歌与时代》(1980)等。他的诗歌融合了东西方传统，探讨了身份、语言和存在等哲学主题。1990年，帕斯被授予诺贝尔文学奖，表彰他'充满激情的诗歌作品，以宽广的视野洞悉人类状况，将墨西哥与拉丁美洲的斗争与体验融入普遍的文明之中'。获奖后，他的国际影响力进一步扩大，成为墨西哥文化的重要代表。晚年，他继续写作和思考，关注全球化背景下的文化身份问题，直到1998年在墨西哥城逝世，享年84岁。
points.descriptionEn: After 1976, Paz returned to Mexico City, focusing on literary creation and academic research. This period marked the peak of his creative output, with the publication of major works including 'East Slope' (1976), 'The Turn' (1977), and 'Poetry and Time' (1980). His poetry blended Eastern and Western traditions, exploring philosophical themes of identity, language, and existence. In 1990, Paz was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature, which recognized 'passionate poetry with wide horizons, insight into human existence, and the integration of Mexican and Latin American struggles and experiences into universal civilization.' After winning the prize, his international influence grew further, making him an important representative of Mexican culture. In his later years, he continued to write and reflect on issues of cultural identity in the context of globalization until his death in Mexico City in 1998 at the age of 84.

supporter.zh: 帕斯被誉为墨西哥最伟大的诗人之一，他的作品深刻影响了拉丁美洲文学的发展。支持者认为他成功地将墨西哥土著文化、欧洲现代主义和东方哲学融为一体，创造了独特的文学风格。他创办的《多元》杂志成为墨西哥知识界的重要平台，培养了新一代作家和思想家。帕斯对墨西哥身份认同的探索超越了民族主义，提出了普遍的人文关怀，使他成为连接东西方文化的桥梁。他的诺贝尔文学奖不仅是对个人成就的肯定，也是对整个拉丁美洲文学的认可。
supporter.en: Paz is regarded as one of Mexico's greatest poets, and his work has profoundly influenced the development of Latin American literature. Supporters believe he successfully blended Mexican indigenous culture, European modernism, and Eastern philosophy to create a unique literary style. The magazine 'Vuelta' that he founded became an important platform for Mexican intellectuals, nurturing a new generation of writers and thinkers. Paz's exploration of Mexican identity transcended nationalism, offering universal humanistic concerns, making him a bridge between Eastern and Western cultures. His Nobel Prize was not only recognition of his personal achievements but also an acknowledgment of Latin American literature as a whole.

critic.zh: 批评者指出帕斯的作品过于精英主义，脱离了墨西哥普通民众的现实生活。他早期对土著文化的浪漫化描述被批评为简化了复杂的种族和文化问题。在政治立场上，帕斯虽然批评墨西哥的一党专政，但也被认为过于依赖西方思想框架，未能充分发展出替代性的拉丁美洲政治理论。一些左翼批评者认为他在特莱蒂洛科事件后的政治立场不够坚定，有时过于温和。此外，他的诗歌被批评为过于抽象和晦涩，缺乏与读者的直接情感连接。
critic.en: Critics point out that Paz's work is overly elitist, disconnected from the everyday realities of ordinary Mexicans. His early romanticized portrayals of indigenous culture have been criticized for simplifying complex racial and cultural issues. Politically, although he criticized Mexico's one-party system, he is also seen as overly dependent on Western intellectual frameworks, failing to develop alternative Latin American political theories. Some leftist critics argue that his political stance after the Tlatelolco event was not firm enough, sometimes too moderate. Additionally, his poetry has been criticized as too abstract and obscure, lacking direct emotional connection with readers.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，帕斯被定义为墨西哥现代文化的象征人物，他的作品反映了20世纪拉丁美洲知识分子对身份、现代性和全球化的思考。他既是墨西哥民族文化的守护者，又是世界主义的倡导者，这种双重身份使他成为全球化时代文化对话的重要人物。帕斯的文学成就和政治立场使他成为墨西哥知识分子的典范，他的思想影响了整整一代拉丁美洲作家和思想家。在当代文化讨论中，帕斯关于语言、翻译和跨文化对话的观点仍然具有重要的参考价值，他的作品被广泛翻译和研究，成为世界文学的重要组成部分。
objective.en: In academic and popular culture, Paz is defined as a symbolic figure of Mexican modern culture, and his work reflects 20th-century Latin American intellectuals' reflections on identity, modernity, and globalization. He was both a guardian of Mexican national culture and an advocate of cosmopolitanism, making him an important figure in cultural dialogue in the age of globalization. Paz's literary achievements and political stance have made him a model for Mexican intellectuals, and his thoughts have influenced generations of Latin American writers and thinkers. In contemporary cultural discussions, Paz's views on language, translation, and cross-cultural dialogue remain highly relevant, and his works are widely translated and studied, forming an important part of world literature.

self.zh: 诗歌不是情感的宣泄，而是情感的发现。
self.en: Poetry is not the expression of emotion but the discovery of emotion.

others.zh: 帕斯是一位真正的世界公民，他的诗歌超越了地理和政治边界，探索人类共同的经验和情感。
others.en: Paz was a true citizen of the world; his poetry transcended geographical and political boundaries to explore the common experiences and emotions of humanity.
